decision.reason: Evaluated specifically against Fang et al. (2008, 10.1167/8.7.2), the replication outcome is genuinely mixed. De-Wit et al. (2012) confirm Fang 2008's reduced V1 (F(15,150)=6.24, p<0.001) and V2 (F(15,135)=6.93, p<0.001) responses and null V3 response (F(15,120)=0.92, p=0.542) during the global diamond percept, as well as increased activation in posterior LO (F(15,150)=3.96, p<0.001) and weaker non-significant modulation in anterior pFs/TOA (F(15,150)=0.74, p=0.7). However, two Fang-specific findings/claims do not hold: (1) whereas Fang 2008 localized only predefined stimulus ROIs (fang_pku.txt chars 10256-11527) and did not measure off-stimulus V1, Fang 2008 explicitly claimed in Discussion (p. 6, chars 16131-17093) that V1 modulation occurred in the stimulus representation 'and not in immediately adjacent retinotopic regions,' which de-Wit et al. directly test and disconfirm by finding equal modulation across unstimulated Background and Conservative-Background V1/V2 ROIs (edb96f4b87f5413a.txt chars 10443-11237, 24115-29608, 34108-34846); and (2) de-Wit et al.'s combined LOC (LO+pFs) ROI was null (F(15,150)=1.23, p=0.236; chars 31135-32092), with reconciliation to Fang's LOC/TOA relying only on personal communication rather than verified mask equivalence.

In the Diamond runs participants were presented
with 16 seconds of ﬁxation at the start of the run
followed by 403 seconds of the bistable moving
diamond / lines stimulus followed by a further 13
seconds of ﬁxation. Participants had to ﬁxate on a
small central dot during the entire run. The Diamond
stimulus consisted of four oriented lines that moved
such that they could be interpreted either as four lines
moving separately (local condition) or as one solid
(‘diamond’) shape moving horizontally behind three
invisible occluding bars (global condition; Figure 1).
decision.reason: Both shipped and blind coding classify type as 'replication'. De-Wit et al. (2012) collected new fMRI data from 13 newly tested participants at the University of Leuven (12 analyzed after excluding 1 participant lacking baseline fixation normalization; final ROI samples: 11 for V1 and LOC, 10 for V2, 9 for V3; edb96f4b87f5413a.txt chars 11727-13876, 17912-23532). Although Meridian-Mapping, Object-Versus-Scrambled-Object localizer, and T1 structural scans were available from a prior study (Kubilius et al., 2011) for 6 of the participants, all 13 participants completed new Diamond, Stimulus-Specific-Checkerboard, and Large-Square-Wave-Grating experimental fMRI runs testing the bistable diamond paradigm of Fang et al. (2008) and Murray et al. (2002, Experiment 3) in an independent sample.

None of the SNPs was significantly associated with NOA (P > 0.05). However, three of four SNPs (rs12097821, rs2477686, and rs10842262) showed associations in the same direction in Japanese men as those reported in the Chinese GWAS. To determine whether the four SNPs are genetic risk factors for NOA, the effect sizes of NOA risk factors require further investigation using larger independent sets of case-control samples of populations, including Japanese and Chinese populations.
decision.reason: Primary Table 1 and Figure 2 of Hu et al. (2011, 10.1038/ng.1040; hu_table.txt, hu_figure.txt) confirm that the bound original Chinese GWAS (N=2,927 cases, 5,734 controls) reported combined genome-wide significant NOA associations (P<5e-8) across all four exact SNPs: rs12097821 (OR=1.25), rs2477686 (OR=1.39), rs10842262 (OR=1.23)—all three replicated in Validation I and II—and rs6080550 (combined OR=1.27, P=2.17e-9, though non-significant in Validation II, OR=1.13, P=0.10). Sato et al. (2013, 2b4faa1d0d497c42.txt; complete abstract, with pages 2-4 unavailable) tested all four SNPs across two Japanese cohorts (490 NOA patients, 1,167 controls) combined by meta-analysis specifically 'to evaluate whether SNP loci are associated with NOA' and 'To assess the significance of the associations'. In the meta-analysis, 'None of the SNPs was significantly associated with NOA (P > 0.05)' (rs12097821 OR=1.10, CI=0.89-1.37; rs2477686 OR=1.11, CI=0.87-1.43; rs10842262 OR=1.11, CI=0.94-1.32; rs6080550 OR=0.96, CI=0.76-1.21). Under the codebook, non-significant same-direction point estimates on three SNPs do not constitute partial replication ('mixed'), and requesting larger future studies to determine whether the SNPs are risk factors does not make a completed meta-analysis 'uninformative' or 'cannot_determine'.

decision.reason: Recovered Bock & Loebell (1990, 10.1016/0010-0277(90)90035-i; pubmed.raw, 39-page PDF, original.pdftotext.txt) shows that while pp. 17 and 35-36 acknowledge locative/beneficiary goal overlap (addressed via Experiment 2's passive/locative test) and allow thematic linking to grammatical roles before constituent formation (Bock et al., 1989/1992), the original explicitly claimed for the explored oblique-phrase domain that predicate/constituent structures ('[NP [V NP PP]]' vs. '[NP [V NP NP]]') are 'devoid of thematic content' and 'insulated from the elaboration of constituents' (p. 35), so event-structure changes do not alter phrase-structure persistence (Abstract, Experiment 1). Also, the intransitive baseline cited by Hare & Goldberg traces to Bock (1986, Experiment 1; 1990 pp. 16-17), not a tested 1990 condition, and original locative, passive/by-locative, and infinitive controls were not rerun. In Hare & Goldberg (f4ef4cba54e4ea6b.txt), the retested Experiment 1 ditransitive vs. prepositional-dative contrast replicates (87% vs. 55% ditransitive responses, 32% difference, p<.01 for subjects and items), and the authors affirm that syntactic form contributes alongside semantics (not 'statistically_successful_but_flawed'). However, pitting '[NP V NP PP]' syntax against '<agent, recipient, theme>' role order in 'provide-with' primes yields 83% ditransitives (p<.05 vs. dative, p>.1 vs. ditransitive, ruling out simple additive animacy), disconfirming thematic-role-independent '[NP V NP PP]' phrase-structure priming ('The structural prime only has an effect only when it combines both the syntax and the semantics of the prepositional dative', p. 210), supporting 'mixed'.
